title: Cellular Biomechanics & Mechanobiology
description: Connect forces, matrix mechanics, cell adhesion, mechanotransduction, and quantitative assays across molecular-to-tissue scales.

prerequisites.statement: Cell biology; Physics: Mechanics; Differential Equations recommended

outcomes.description: Translate boundary conditions into stress and strain measures.
Interpret viscoelastic and nonlinear material behavior.
Connect integrin/cytoskeletal signaling to mechanical context.
Design an experiment that separates stiffness from ligand density.

lesson_objectives.description: Distinguish force, stress, displacement, and strain.
Select a constitutive model appropriate to the time and strain regime.
Trace a force path from extracellular matrix to nucleus.
Predict how adhesion geometry changes local signaling.
Distinguish a mechanical input from a molecular readout.
Use perturbation and rescue to support a pathway mechanism.
Separate matrix mechanics from ligand presentation and geometry.
Choose analysis that respects nested replicates and batch structure.

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: Stress, strain, and constitutive behavior
lessons.worked_example: A standard linear solid can relax toward a nonzero long-time modulus, unlike a Maxwell element that relaxes fully under an ideal step strain.

lessons.title: Adhesion, cytoskeleton, and force transmission
lessons.worked_example: A stiffer substrate can increase traction only under conditions where cells can engage and remodel adhesions; stiffness alone does not specify cell fate.

lessons.title: Mechanotransduction and mechanosensitive pathways
lessons.worked_example: If inhibiting a mechanosensitive channel blocks calcium entry and a downstream transcriptional response, channel-specific rescue or an orthogonal perturbation strengthens the causal chain.

lessons.title: Experimental design for cell mechanics
lessons.worked_example: A 2×2 stiffness-by-ligand-density design estimates both main effects and interaction, provided each combination is independently fabricated and randomized across runs.
